html:
The Russo-Turkish War of 1877 to 1878 was a war in which Russia, with Romania and Bulgarian volunteers, defeated the Ottoman Empire and ended Ottoman rule over most of Bulgaria.

Russia declared war in April 1877 after the crushing of the April Uprising. The Russians held the Shipka Pass against Ottoman attacks and took the fortress of Plevna after a long siege, then marched almost to Constantinople. The Treaty of San Stefano of 3 March 1878 created a large Bulgaria, but the powers cut it down at the Congress of Berlin months later, leaving Macedonia to the Ottomans. 3 March is Bulgaria's national day. The war also won independence for Romania, Serbia and Montenegro.
sum: The Russo-Turkish War of 1877 to 1878 was a war in which Russia, with Romania and Bulgarian volunteers, defeated the Ottoman Empire and ended Ottoman rule over most of Bulgaria.
